final_message:
I fixed the bug, and the full suite now passes, including your new test (25 tests).

**Root cause:** `BillingEngine.__init__` in `billing/engine.py` built its context with `dunning_policy and DEFAULT_POLICY`. When no policy was passed, that evaluated to `None`. Then `record_failure` in `dunning.py` tried to read `retry_offsets_days` from `None`, which raised the `TypeError`. A custom policy would also have been silently replaced by the default. I changed `and` to `or`.

I added your test as `tests/test_dunning_regression.py` and wrote `answer.json` as `{"file": "engine.py", "function": "__init__"}`.

steps.command: ls billing && wc -l billing/*.py && cat tests/conftest.py && grep -n "card\|def \|dunning\|past_due" billing/engine.py | head -150

sed -i 's/dunning_policy and DEFAULT_POLICY/dunning_policy or DEFAULT_POLICY/' billing/engine.py && echo '{"file": "engine.py", "function": "__init__"}' > answer.json && cat >> tests/test_dunning_regression.py <<'EOF'


def test_customer_without_card_enters_dunning(world):
    cus = world.customer(card=False)
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["attempt_count"] == 1
    assert inv["next_attempt_at"] is not None
    assert sub["status"] == "past_due"
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8

sed -i '' 's/dunning_policy and DEFAULT_POLICY/dunning_policy or DEFAULT_POLICY/' billing/engine.py && echo '{"file": "engine.py", "function": "__init__"}' > answer.json && cat > tests/test_dunning_regression.py <<'EOF'
def test_customer_without_card_enters_dunning(world):
    cus = world.customer(card=False)
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["attempt_count"] == 1
    assert inv["next_attempt_at"] is not None
    assert sub["status"] == "past_due"
EOF
git diff --stat; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8
